correctness.rationale: The elementary disjoint-pair event has exact probability product of reciprocal remaining-stub counts. Every matching has uniform residual law after conditioning on the r cross-vertex pairs. The residual eligible same-vertex pairs are n*binom(d,2)-r*(2d-r-1), giving E[L P_r]/E[P_r]; subtract E[L] to obtain the exact claimed covariance. Denominators are strictly positive for n>=3, d>=2, 2<=r<=d and nd even. The bracket equals d-1 at saturation, and is at most 2d-r-1-3d<0 below saturation. Exact all-pairing enumeration with Fraction agrees for nd<=12; fixed-d leading terms are derived analytically.

value.rationale: The joint behavior of loops and parallel-edge defects controls when the configuration model departs from simplicity. The exact sign of that dependence is not predicted by asymptotic independent-Poisson laws. The all-r natural factorial-multiplicity spectrum exhibits a structural, strict reversal only at complete saturation of endpoint stubs, with a distinct n^(-d) positive finite-size order versus negative n^(1-r) unsaturated effects. This is a motivated full classification of an intrinsic model statistic, not a numerical or arbitrary slice.
